slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Vouvray (Touraine) is home to one of the world's few AOCs that can produce everything from bone-dry whites to botrytis sweet wines and traditional-method sparkling wines, all from a single appellation. Its diversity comes from one variety — Chenin Blanc — and the Tuffeau tuffstone, a breathable bedrock.

Course Learning Objectives

📐 Four-Tier Sweetness System

Fully master the residual sugar standards and tasting characteristics of Sec / Demi-Sec / Moelleux / Liquoreux

🪨 Tuffeau Tuffstone Terroir

Understand how this porous chalky bedrock brings mineral depth and aging potential to Chenin Blanc

🍇 Three Sweet Wine Production Methods

Distinguish between botrytis (Botrytis), vine-drying (Passerillage), and late harvest (Tries)

🥂 Vouvray Mousseux / Pétillant

Learn about Vouvray's traditional-method sparkling wine — one of France's leading bottle-fermented sparkling regions after Champagne
slides.1.title: Vouvray — The Full-Spectrum Stage for Chenin Blanc
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Tuffeau Tuffstone
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Porous chalky bedrock formed in the Late Cretaceous — the classic terroir of the central Loire
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Single Variety
slides.1.highlights.1.content: 100% Chenin Blanc; no blending with other varieties permitted
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sweetness Spectrum
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The same AOC can produce four sweetness levels — Sec / Demi-Sec / Moelleux / Liquoreux — plus sparkling
slides.1.content:
Vouvray is east of Tours, on the north bank of the Loire River. The AOC spans 8 villages: Vouvray, Vernou-sur-Brenne, Sainte-Radegonde, Rochecorbon, Chançay, Noizay, Reugny, Parçay-Meslay. Most vineyards are planted on Tuffeau bedrock on high river bank slopes, which also contain extensive 19th-century cave cellars (Cave Troglodyte).

📐 Vouvray Key Facts

  • Area: ~2,200 ha
  • Variety: 100% Chenin Blanc
  • Soils: Tuffeau tuffstone, Aubuis (clay-limestone), Perruches (clay-flint)
  • Climate: Mild continental, moderated by the Loire River
  • Annual production: ~120,000 hL, of which ~60% is sparkling
  • Sparkling labels: Vouvray Mousseux (traditional method), Vouvray Pétillant (lightly sparkling, 3.5–4 atm)
slides.1.quiz.question: What variety does the Vouvray AOC require?
slides.1.quiz.explanation: Vouvray is a single-variety AOC for Chenin Blanc, with no blending of other varieties permitted. This rule ensures that all Vouvray purely reflects Chenin's response to terroir and vintage conditions; the different sweetness levels and sparkling styles all come entirely from winemaking choices and vintage conditions.
slides.3.title: Tuffeau Tuffstone — A Breathing Bedrock
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Porous and Moisture-Absorbing
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Porosity up to 45%; can absorb and release moisture, regulating water availability in the vine root zone
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Castle Building Material
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The snow-white walls of Loire châteaux (Chambord, Chenonceau, etc.) are cut blocks of Tuffeau
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Underground Wine Cellars
slides.3.highlights.2.content: 19th-century quarrying tunnels became natural wine cellars, maintaining a constant 12°C and 85% humidity
slides.3.content:
Tuffeau is the key terroir shared by Vouvray, Montlouis, Saumur, Chinon, and other Loire mid-valley appellations. It was formed during the Late Cretaceous (Turonian period, ~90 million years ago) in shallow marine deposits, composed mainly of foraminifera, sponge spicules, and quartz sand cemented together — soft, snow-white, and highly porous.

🌊 Formation and Structure

  • Late Cretaceous shallow marine deposits, rich in calcium carbonate (50–60%)
  • Porosity up to 45%, soft texture and easy to cut
  • Two types: Tuffeau Blanc (white) and Tuffeau Jaune (yellow, containing glass sponge spicules)

🌱 Effect on Vines

  • Water regulation: Porous structure retains water without waterlogging, allowing vine roots to absorb water steadily even in drought years
  • Mineral supply: Rich in calcium carbonate, giving Chenin a chalky mineral tension
  • Temperature moderation: White surface reflects sunlight, moderating high temperatures during the ripening period

🍷 Effect on Flavor

  • Chalky mineral texture, wet stone, beeswax, chamomile
  • High acid structure (pH typically 3.0–3.2)
  • 10+ year aging potential; develops stewed apple, toasted hazelnut, foie gras flavors
slides.3.quiz.question: Tuffeau tuffstone's porosity of up to 45% — what is its primary effect on viticulture?
slides.3.quiz.options.0: Makes it difficult for vine roots to penetrate
slides.3.quiz.options.1: Absorbs and releases water, providing steady water supply to vines in drought years
slides.3.quiz.explanation: Tuffeau's high porosity (45%) makes it like a natural sponge — absorbing water when it rains, then slowly releasing it to the vine root zone during dry periods. This is especially critical during extreme drought years like 2003, 2018, and 2022, allowing Vouvray's Chenin Blanc to maintain balanced acidity and ripeness even in dry years. This characteristic also makes Tuffeau an ideal wine cellar material.
slides.5.title: Vouvray Sparkling — A Forgotten French Sparkling Wine Treasure
slides.5.highlights.0.title: Traditional Method Production
slides.5.highlights.0.content: Vouvray Mousseux follows the same regulations as Méthode Champenoise (bottle-fermented secondary fermentation)
slides.5.highlights.1.title: Two Pressure Levels
slides.5.highlights.1.content: Mousseux (5 atm, fully sparkling) and Pétillant (3.5 atm, lightly sparkling) coexist
slides.5.highlights.2.title: Remarkable Production Volume
slides.5.highlights.2.content: 60% of Vouvray's production is sparkling — one of France's leading bottle-fermented regions after Champagne and Limoux
slides.5.content:
Many people don't know that Vouvray's sparkling wine production far exceeds its still wine output — this traces back to the late 19th century, when Chenin's high-acid character combined with the convenience of railway transport made Vouvray an affordable alternative to Champagne on Parisian dining tables. Today's Vouvray Mousseux/Pétillant continues this tradition, representing the highest benchmark for Chenin Blanc sparkling wine.

🥂 Vouvray Mousseux (5 atm)

  • Bottle-fermented secondary fermentation (Méthode Traditionnelle)
  • Minimum 9 months lees aging (most estates 12–24 months)
  • Style: green apple, white flowers, toasted bread, chalky minerality
  • Common: Brut (<12 g/L residual sugar), Sec, Demi-Sec

🫧 Vouvray Pétillant (3.5 atm)

  • Lightly sparkling style (closer to Frizzante)
  • Fine bubbles, softer mouthfeel
  • Traditional food-pairing wine; great with pork charcuterie, white sauce dishes

🌟 Key Producers

  • Domaine Huet (King of Vouvray): Pétillant series especially classic; Le Mont Pétillant can age 20+ years
  • François Pinon: Organic natural wine style; Brut Non Dosé extremely pure
  • Vincent Carême: New-generation representative; Ancestrale (Pét-Nat) returns to ancestral method
  • Domaine de la Taille aux Loups: Jacky Blot spans Vouvray + Montlouis
slides.6.title: Level 3-6 Knowledge Test
slides.6.questions.0.question: What is the residual sugar range for Demi-Sec in Vouvray AOC?
slides.6.questions.0.explanation: Vouvray sweetness classification: Sec (<4 g/L), Sec-Tendre (4–8 g/L), Demi-Sec (12–45 g/L), Moelleux (45–80 g/L), Liquoreux (>80 g/L). Demi-Sec is the most representative style of Vouvray, often considered the most natural expression of Chenin Blanc and Tuffeau terroir.
slides.6.questions.1.question: Approximately what percentage of Vouvray's production is sparkling wine?
slides.6.questions.1.explanation: Approximately 60% of Vouvray's production is sparkling wine (Mousseux + Pétillant), making it one of France's most important bottle-fermented sparkling regions after Champagne. This tradition dates to the late 19th century, when railways transported Vouvray's high-acid Chenin to Paris as an affordable alternative to Champagne.
slides.6.questions.2.question: How does Vouvray primarily accumulate sugar in its sweet wines? (Select the most common method)
slides.6.questions.2.explanation: Vouvray's Moelleux and Liquoreux are primarily produced through Botrytis cinerea (noble rot) infection. The Loire River and Brenne Valley create morning mists in autumn (inducing noble rot) and afternoon drying sunshine (preventing harmful grey rot), providing ideal noble rot conditions. Secondary methods include Passerillage (vine-drying) and multiple pickings (Tries). AOC rules strictly prohibit chaptalization for sweet wine grades.
slides.6.questions.3.question: What is the formation period and main composition of Tuffeau tuffstone?
slides.6.questions.3.options.0: Late Jurassic, containing Exogyra oyster fossils
slides.6.questions.3.options.1: Late Cretaceous, containing calcium carbonate and sponge spicules
slides.6.questions.3.explanation: Tuffeau was formed during the Late Cretaceous (Turonian period, ~90 million years ago), with main components of calcium carbonate (50–60%), glass sponge spicules, and quartz sand. It is completely different from the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian (Sancerre/Chablis soils), which explains the stark contrast in styles between central Loire Chenin/Sauvignon and central Loire proper.
